subject: recency-selection
kind: deliver
result: pass
revision: 1643ae678f3f2352402747f472f60cfb5d7580b6
evidence:
- TDD: I added the tests first. Before the change, 7 new tests failed and 14 passed. Several malformed-window cases passed early only because `within` was still an unknown operator.
- `cd ~/aa-wt-recency-selection && python3 -m pytest tools/runtime/tests -q` gave `410 passed, 59 subtests passed in 37.16s`.
- `python3 design/contracts/validate.py` still passes. The incident-response, ml-research and parcelpipe fixtures resolve as before.
- Commit: `feat(selection): match recorded_at within a relative window`.
- Files changed:
  - `tools/runtime/contract.py`: adds `within` to `SELECTION_OPERATORS`, adds `WINDOW_PATTERN` and `parse_window()`, validates the window in `_validate_role_selection`, and gives `record_matches_selection(record, selection, now=None)` an injectable `now` that defaults to the current UTC time.
  - `design/contracts/resolve.py`: `validate_selection` (contract resolution) gets the same operator and window checks, raising `ResolveError`.
  - `design/contracts/README.md`: documents the new clause in the predicate-grammar section.
  - `tools/runtime/tests/test_selection_operators.py`: new `RecencyWindowTests`, new resolve-validation cases, and a new `ContractLoadValidationTests`.
- Clause syntax: `{"field": "recorded_at", "within": "24h"}`.
  - The window is a positive integer plus a unit `m`, `h` or `d`, matched by the regex `[1-9][0-9]*[mhd]`.
  - These values are rejected: "24x", "", "-24h", "0h", "h", "24", 24, None, "1.5h", " 24h".
  - `within` works only on `recorded_at`, and `recorded_at` accepts only `within`. Any other pairing fails both at resolution and at contract load.
- Matching behaviour: a record matches when `recorded_at >= now - window`. A record with no `recorded_at` never matches. Acceptance test: with a 24h window, a record from 1h ago matches and a record from 48h ago does not.
- I did not touch `handoff.py`. Its `_select_records` calls `record_matches_selection` without `now`, so rendering uses the current time.
observations:
- Stale-view risk: `_store_state_digest` / `live_view_state_digest` in `handoff.py` hash store contents only. A time-window role can gain or lose records as time passes with no record write. The staleness check will not flag it, so a rendered view can quietly drift. I did not redesign the digests.
- The allowed operators and fields are listed twice, in `contract.py` and in `design/contracts/resolve.py`. `resolve.py` says the two must be changed together. I updated both, but the regex is copied, not shared.
- `datetime.fromisoformat` raises on a malformed `recorded_at`, and a naive timestamp breaks the comparison with the timezone-aware `now`. The runtime `_now()` always writes timestamps like `2026-09-29T12:00:00+00:00`, so records it writes are safe. Hand-edited records could still hit this.
- The docstring at the top of `tools/runtime/query.py` was already out of date: it says `record_matches_selection` supports only literal equality. I left it unchanged.
